items.t: Crop model 11.63m bales vs USDA 13.44m (-14%), driven by Texas abandonment of 52% vs USDA's 34% on drought and poor ratings. A cut that size after the October report has happened once since 2010/11 (2020/21, -14%), so the model sits near the edge of history.

Watch: West Texas-Kansas-Oklahoma (production estimates falling, fiber quality concerns, regrowth, insurance adjusters in fields, some gins not opening); Desert Southwest (DSW) (storm damage being assessed); American Pima (AP) (storm damage being assessed). India's crop looks like 21.0 m bales on the desk model (USDA 24.0) after the driest June–September in its main cotton districts since at least 1991. With the import duty waived to 2026-12-31 India imports about 4.5 m bales (5.3 m if the waiver runs all season) vs USDA's 3.3 m. US cotton to India: 0.9–1.5 m bales against 0.28 m committed, so 0.7–1.2 m of new US sales are still to come. Counting the Brazilian, African and Australian cotton India takes from other buyers, US exports gain about 0.4 m bales in the desk base and 1.0 m in the bearish (big-crop, lower-price) case; in the desk's simulated balance sheet (crop and exports drawn together, India's duty path included) base exports are 12.9 m vs USDA 12.3, ending stocks 2.3 m (bullish 1.5, bearish 3.9; USDA 3.80), and 89% of runs end below USDA. At today's prices more of this demand gets booked. History says the market prices this through what USDA reports by February–March: if USDA's March US stocks/use reaches the desk base, May, May/Jul (-0.72) and Jul/Dec (+6.66) are all cheap (see Price and spreads); Mar/May (-1.63) has stayed a carry outside world-shortage years.
Desk base case 2026/27 ending stocks 2.32 vs USDA 3.80 (stocks/use 16.1% vs 27.5%); bearish 3.86, bullish 1.50.

May is 83.70. Simulating every combination of crop, exports, India's duty path and historical fit, May averages 105 in February–March (70–156, 10th–90th percentile), with a 75% chance it trades 90 or higher by mid-March and 27% that it trades 78 or lower first. Merchants' shorts are 54% of world exports, the most at this time of year since 2010/11; in heavily hedged seasons May rose 19% on average. Fair value in February–March, when USDA's numbers settle: if USDA's March US stocks/use reaches the desk base (16%), May is worth 95–105, May/Jul +0.7 to +1.8 and Jul/Dec +12 to +15; on USDA's 27.5% they are about 76, -0.6 and +2. Today's prices imply a March number near 24% (May) and 22% (Jul/Dec). Mar/May -1.63 has stayed a carry outside world-shortage years. Open interest has already moved forward: May and Jul hold 97k lots, a record for this date since 2000 (median 20k; 24% of the total vs 11%), so less rolls out of Dec and hedge-lifting as mills fix lands in May and Jul. Downside is limited by who sells: growers are well hedged and can hold cotton in the 55¢ loan, producer fixations are modest and merchants are hedged, so funds are the main seller, against 42k lots mills still have to fix; with a book this size May's worst drop to mid-March has averaged -6% (about 79; worst 74).
